sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources (primary, read this session):** SMFG "Investor Meeting FY3/2026" presentation (May 18, 2026, smfg.co.jp/english/investor/financial/latest_statement/2026_3/2026_fy_e_summary.pdf) — pages cited by content below since PDF page numbers shifted on extraction; BOJ policy statement June 16, 2026 (boj.or.jp k260616a.pdf) and follow-on commentary; SMFG equity-holdings policy page (smfg.co.jp/english/company/organization/governance/structure/hold.html); the market-parameter file (JPY policy-rate proxy, asof 2026-06-16).

**Sustainable ROE build (NIM × leverage − credit cost − opex, capital-constrained growth):**
- FY3/26 (year ended Mar-31-2026) actual: consolidated net income JPY1,583.0bn (+JPY405.0bn YoY, JPY83.0bn ahead of the raised target), statutory ROE 10.4% (hit the prior medium-term plan's 10% target), managerial-basis ROTE 11.4%.
- New medium-term plan (announced with this presentation, launched Apr-2026) sets ROTE 13% as an FY3/29 milestone en route to a "medium-to-long-term" 15% ROTE aspiration (net income raised to the mid-JPY2tn level, from JPY1,583bn FY3/26 / JPY1,700bn FY3/27 target) — explicitly benchmarked against JPMorgan/HSBC/BofA/Goldman/Barclays 14-18% ROTE peer targets. I treat 13% by FY3/29 as the credible underwrite level and 15% as optionality, not base case (large developed-market banks rarely clear self-set 3-year-out ROE bridges in full — see pre-mortem).
- Rate-driven NIM path (the core mechanism): SMBC's domestic loan-to-deposit spread (managerial basis) was 1.14% for FY3/26, up +18bp YoY, and — critically — accelerated intra-year from 1.10% in 1H to 1.17% in 2H as the deposit book re-priced with a lag behind the loan book (interest earned on loans 1.34%, +32bp YoY; interest paid on deposits only 0.20%, +14bp YoY — i.e., deposit beta materially <1 so far). Management's own sensitivity: a further +25bp BOJ hike adds ~JPY110bn to NII in year 1, building to ~JPY150bn by year 5 as the fixed-rate back book reprices — this is a multi-year, not one-time, tailwind as long as BOJ keeps hiking and deposit beta stays lagged.
- BOJ policy path (verified this session, not just carried from macro memo): BOJ hiked to 1.00% on 2026-06-16 (31-year high), market pricing a hold at the Jul-30/31 2026 meeting; board member Tamura's stated baseline is +25bp every few months toward a ~2% neutral rate, with most outside forecasters penciling the next hike (to 1.25%) by end-2026. SMFG's own house planning assumption for the medium-to-long-term ROTE target uses Japan policy rate 1.25% / US 3.0% — i.e., management is underwriting only ~1 more hike from here, not the full run to neutral. If BOJ tracks Tamura's faster path, the NII sensitivity above is a source of upside optionality against SMFG's own plan, not something I need to assume to justify entry.
- Credit costs (through-cycle, not latest quarter, per method card): consolidated total credit cost JPY210.2bn (FY3/23) → 274.0bn (FY3/24) → 344.5bn (FY3/25) → 388.4bn (FY3/26); FY3/27 guided down to JPY340bn. Against consolidated loans of JPY111.2tn (Mar-26), FY3/26 credit cost ratio ≈ 35bp — but this is inflated by idiosyncratic items management called out explicitly: a JPY31bn disposal of a specific NPL exposure ("OTO/SOF"), provisions against several large overseas borrowers including Brazil exposure, and a forward-looking (not-yet-realized) provision taken for potential Middle East spillover risk. Consolidated NPL ratio jumped to 0.97% at Mar-26 from 0.67% at Mar-25 (SMBC-only NPL ratio rose a smaller 0.43%→0.71%), which is the flag to watch, but the balance-of-evidence attribution is overseas/EM-book-specific rather than a domestic Japan credit-cycle turn — domestic claims-requiring-caution and NPL trends are not described as deteriorating. I underwrite a through-cycle credit cost of ~30bp (below the FY3/26 print, above the FY3/23-24 average) given the overseas multi-franchise strategy (India/SMICC, Brazil, Vietnam-VPBank/FE Credit, US) structurally adds credit-cost variance versus a pure domestic megabank — this is a real cost of the growth strategy, not a rounding error.
- Opex: overhead ratio 54.7% FY3/26 (-3.5pp YoY, i.e., positive operating leverage from gross profit +717.9bn outpacing G&A +249.6bn); medium-term target is "low-50%" range by FY3/29 via cost discipline + IT-driven efficiency (JPY1tn IT investment over 3 years, ~20bp CET1 drag).
- Capital constraint on growth: CET1 ratio (finalized Basel III, transitional, including OCI) 11.1% at Mar-26 (10.3% excluding unrealized securities gains); target raised 50bp to ~10.5% (10.0-11.0% band) by Mar-29 specifically citing geopolitical risk and the shrinking OCI cushion as cross-shareholdings are sold down. Payout: dividend payout ratio target held at 40% with a newly hardened "increase every year" commitment; historical total payout ratio (dividends + buybacks) has run 51-61% since FY3/24. DPS has grown JPY122 (FY3/25) → JPY157 (FY3/26) → JPY180 guided (FY3/27), i.e., +29% then +15%. Using ROTE ~11-13% and a ~55% total payout, sustainable book-value growth g ≈ ROTE×(1-payout) ≈ 11-13%×0.45 ≈ 5-6%: this is a re-rating-plus-distribution thesis, not a growth-compounding one — SMFG is capital-return-constrained by choice (buybacks/dividends), not CET1-constrained (CET1 sits comfortably inside the new target band).

**Earnings-quality gate (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS — banks: provisioning-vs-write-off trend, not accruals ratio):**
- Provisioning/write-off 3y trend: credit cost has risen every year for 4 years (210→274→345→388 JPY bn, FY3/23-26) while FY3/27 is guided down (340bn) — management is building provisions ahead of/alongside a modest NPL uptick rather than being caught behind it (forward-looking Middle East provision taken pre-emptively, not after a loss event) — this reads as conservative-to-neutral, not aggressive under-provisioning. No divergence found between margin expansion and cash conversion — the +212bn YoY "core business" profit growth is stated net of one-off and rate/FX effects.
- Cash-conversion trend: not separately disclosed at group level in this presentation; no capitalized-cost creep found in the materials reviewed — none found, checked (flagged as a limited-evidence "none found" rather than an exhaustive audit).
- Related-party/cross-shareholding gravity (Sumitomo keiretsu): SMFG discloses "market value of equity holdings (policy-oriented/strategic stock)" as a % of consolidated net assets = 27.5% at Mar-26 (down from 32.9% in recent years), under a JPY600bn book-value reduction plan (FY3/25-FY3/29) already 52% executed (JPY309bn reduced, ahead of the 40%-of-schedule pace), targeting <20% by Mar-29. This is disclosed as an aggregate figure — SMFG does not publicly break out "Sumitomo-group-only" holdings (Sumitomo Corp, Sumitomo Chemical, Sumitomo Realty, NEC, etc.) from the total strategic-shareholding book in the materials reviewed; treated as a disclosure-limitation gap, not a red flag per se, since the aggregate trend is a genuine multi-year reduction under an accelerating, externally-monitored plan.
- Optics-class flag (haircut applied, not auto-kill): FY3/26 gains on sale of stockholdings were JPY446.1bn (partly the cross-shareholding unwind noted above), and management explicitly used one-off profit (equity-sale gains + a subsidiary dividend + a VPBank allowance reversal, ~JPY224bn of one-offs) to fund "future measures" (bond-portfolio de-risking, forward-looking provisions, US subsidiary restructuring losses, ~JPY188bn). This is disclosed transparently in the earnings walk (not hidden), but it means reported net-income growth this year is partly a one-time realization of the strategic-shareholding unwind rather than pure recurring banking profit — I haircut the reported FY3/26 net income/ROE print by treating the "core business, ex one-off, ex rate/FX" +212bn growth figure (management's own clean number) as the more reliable read of underlying momentum, and note this explicitly in the pre-mortem.
- Structure flags: NYSE-listed ADR (Form 20-F foreign private issuer), financials prepared on Japanese GAAP; no trapped-cash/repatriation friction identified — Japan has no capital controls and JPY is freely convertible, so the relevant ADR-specific risk is FX translation on dividends/NAV, not repatriation blockage. Two stock splits in the review window (3-for-1 effective Oct-2024; a further 2-for-1 approved for Oct-2026, DPS after split JPY90) — mechanical, not a quality flag, but a live corporate action to track for order-sizing/entry-level continuity.
- Net gate outcome: no manipulation-class flag found; one optics-class flag (one-off equity-gain contribution to reported profit) — haircut applied above, logged in pre-mortem, does not block the thesis.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: The market narrative on SMFG is that Japan's megabanks are mid-way through a multi-year re-rating as the BOJ exits decades of zero/negative rates, with rising domestic NIMs, buyback-heavy capital return, and unwinding of low-ROE cross-shareholdings pushing P/B up from historically sub-1x levels toward global bank multiples.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Edge taxonomy:** (a) analytical -- original residual-income/warranted-P/BV reconstruction this session (COE build, current-multiple reconstruction from EPS/DPS/ADR-ratio/FX, not taken from a screener); (b) informational-synthesis -- combining scattered primary disclosures (loan-to-deposit spread acceleration intra-year, NPL disaggregation into overseas-specific items, cross-shareholding reduction pace, SMFG's own conservative BOJ terminal-rate planning assumption vs. board member Tamura's faster path) that are not packaged together anywhere. Explicitly NOT claimed: time-arbitrage (no dated catalyst) or structural-flow (no index/flow mechanism identified).

**Market believes:** SMFG (and Japan's megabanks generally) are still early/mid-cycle beneficiaries of BOJ normalization, with ROE improving toward global-peer levels (13-15% ROTE) justifying continued P/BV re-rating -- consistent with the stock's +55% 12-month / +31% 6-month run and sitting at 0% off its 52-week high.

**Why wrong:** The narrative isn't wrong so much as already substantially priced. My own residual-income cross-check (COE 7.8% = JGB 10y ~2.8% + Japan ERP 5.0%; sustainable ROE 11%, below both the FY3/26 actual ROTE of 11.4% and the FY3/29 13% milestone; g~4.5%, capital-constrained) implies a warranted P/BV of ~1.6-1.8x, and that range compresses to ~1.6x at the conservative (5.5%) end of the argued ERP band. My own reconstruction of the CURRENT traded multiple (EPS JPY412 / DPS JPY180 / ADR ratio 0.6 / USDJPY ~161.6, this session) comes out around 1.65-1.75x -- i.e., the re-rating gap that plainly existed when a third-party aggregator still showed P/B near 1.45-1.46x (Feb-2026 snapshot) has mostly closed in the last several months. A well-informed generalist reading the FY3/26 headline (record net income, ROE 10.4% target achieved, EPS +36% YoY) would draw almost exactly the bull case above and would not necessarily net out that ~JPY224bn of the profit beat was one-off (equity-sale gains from the cross-shareholding unwind, a subsidiary dividend, a VPBank allowance reversal) funding ~JPY188bn of "future measures" -- the cleaner core-business growth was JPY212bn, a more modest number. The one piece I'd call genuine (if thin) edge: SMFG's own medium-to-long-term planning assumption for BOJ's terminal rate (1.25%) is more conservative than board member Tamura's stated baseline path toward ~2% neutral -- if BOJ hikes faster than SMFG's own plan, the disclosed NII sensitivity (+JPY110bn yr1, building to +JPY150bn by yr5 per +25bp) is not fully reflected even in management's own targets, let alone in a market view anchored on headlines.

**What proves us wrong:** BOJ pausing or reversing the hiking cycle (domestic recession, yen-crisis intervention, or an inflation undershoot); the NPL ratio (0.97% consolidated at Mar-26, up from 0.67% Mar-25) broadening beyond the disclosed Brazil / Middle-East / OTO-SOF items into the domestic loan book; deposit beta catching up faster than the FY3/26 pattern (competitive repricing eroding the 1.14% loan-to-deposit spread gain); or the FY3/29 13% ROTE milestone being quietly walked back in a future medium-term-plan reset.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts

sections.markdown:
1. Consolidated NPL ratio jumped to 0.97% at Mar-26 from 0.67% at Mar-25 (SMFG "Investor Meeting FY3/2026" presentation, May 18 2026, Asset Quality page) -- a real deterioration signal even though management attributes most of it to specific overseas items (OTO/SOF NPL disposal ~JPY31bn, Brazil-related overseas-borrower provisions, forward-looking Middle-East provisioning).
2. FY3/26 reported net income of JPY1,583.0bn included roughly JPY224bn of one-off profit (equity-sale gains, a subsidiary dividend, a VPBank allowance reversal) against management's own disclosed "core business, ex one-off, ex rate/FX" growth of only JPY212bn (same source, "Breakdown of net income" page) -- the headline beat is not pure organic banking-profit growth.
3. My own reconstructed current traded P/BV (~1.65-1.75x, from EPS JPY412 / DPS JPY180 / ADR ratio 0.6 common share per ADR / USDJPY ~161.6 spot, all sourced this session) is already close to my full warranted range (1.63-1.84x across a 4.5-5.5% Japan ERP band), versus a third-party aggregator print of P/B ~1.45-1.46x as recently as Feb-2026 (macrotrends) -- most of the visible re-rating gap has closed in the last several months.
4. SMFG's own "medium-to-long-term" ROTE aspiration of 15% requires net income near JPY2tn -- roughly +26% above the already-aggressive JPY1.7tn FY3/27 target and +26% above FY3/26 actual of JPY1,583bn -- with no committed date attached (same source, "Our Vision for the Next Five Years and Beyond" page); the credible, dated milestone is the lower FY3/29 13% ROTE target, which I underwrite, not the 15% aspiration.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is mid-2029 (3y horizon end) and this position lost roughly 20-30%. The most likely reason is: the BOJ paused or reversed its hiking cycle during 2027 (a China-adjacent shock, a yen-funding-crisis intervention, or a domestic growth scare from the same global-tariff uncertainty SMFG itself flagged heading into FY3/26), stalling the deposit-beta-lag NII tailwind that is this thesis's core mechanism just as the fixed-rate loan book was mid-reprice. At the same time, the NPL uptick already visible at Mar-26 (0.97% consolidated, on Brazil / Middle-East / OTO-SOF items) broadened as global-macro stress hit SMFG's expanding overseas multi-franchise book (India/SMICC, Brazil, Vietnam), pushing credit costs back toward or above the FY3/26 print instead of down to the FY3/27 JPY340bn guide. Because the market had already re-rated the stock close to its warranted multiple by mid-2026 (per this thesis's own finding that the gap had mostly closed), there was very little valuation cushion -- the P/BV simply marked back down toward 1.2-1.3x on the combination, swamping the still-growing dividend. Secondary risk: the FY3/29 13% ROTE milestone is quietly walked back in a future medium-term-plan reset (a common pattern for multi-year bank ROE targets), removing the re-rating catalyst gradually rather than through one clean, actionable data point.

**BEAR ATTACK — Drew — 2026-07-11T14:47:19Z — VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED**

**0. Fact-check of the load-bearing inputs (verified vs primary/press this session — no fabrication found):**
- FY3/26 net income JPY1,583.0bn — CONFIRMED (SEC 6-K / wires: profit attributable to owners JPY1,582,973m). Caveat: one wire reported net-income growth of +5.5% while the thesis frames +JPY405bn/+34% and "EPS +36%"; the +34% figure is *ordinary* profit — the thesis risks conflating ordinary-profit growth with net-income growth to inflate the "record momentum" optics. Lesser point, not a kill.
- BOJ 1.00% on 2026-06-16, 31-year high, 7-1 vote, more signaled — CONFIRMED (CNBC; Al Jazeera; BOJ k260616a.pdf).
- NII sensitivity — CONFIRMED but SHADED OPTIMISTIC: the company/street figure is ~+JPY100bn per 25bp (S&P Global + multiple wires); the thesis uses +JPY110bn yr1 — ~10% richer than the widely-cited number, nudged in the thesis's own favour.
=> No uncited/fabricated load-bearing input; the fact-check does not itself trigger auto-kill. The trade dies on math and classification below.

**1. Estimates at the widest honest error bar.** Re-run at honest bear inputs: p_up 0.35 (momentum name at 52w high; re-rating admitted "mostly closed"; cost-push hike, see §6), up_pct 18 (mostly ~5-6%/yr book growth, minimal further multiple), down_pct −27 (the thesis's OWN pre-mortem says "lost roughly 20-30%", midpoint, given the EM overseas book). Capital EV = 0.35×18 + 0.65×(−27) = −11.25% over 3y; +6.4 net div/drag = **−4.85% total over 3y** — an absolute loss that trails cash by ~18pp.

**2. Variant perception — a correctly-priced premium, not a mispricing.** The analyst's OWN result is that warranted P/BV (~1.6-1.8x) ≈ current traded P/BV (~1.65-1.75x): price = fair value = no edge for a long. Worse, his fundamental 3-YEAR target ($31.50, ~+22%) sits BELOW the (thin) sell-side 12-MONTH consensus ($28.86, +12%/yr, investing.com, retrieved today) extrapolated over 3y — he is LESS bullish than the street on a name he submits as a long. The only claimed "genuine edge" (SMFG's 1.25% BOJ planning assumption < Tamura's ~2%) IS the consensus japan_reflation trade the whole MOMENTUM sleeve rides (screen: rank 7, factor=japan_reflation, 0% off 52w high after +55%/12m). This is trend-riding dressed as residual income.

**3. Catalyst.** horizon=long, catalyst_date=null — no short catalyst to attack; the BOJ≥1.25%-by-2027-03-31 review is a monitor, not a driver. But the corollary bites: there is no dated event ahead to close a gap the thesis concedes is already "mostly closed." The re-rating is behind us.

**4. Base rate — convenient, not honest.** archetype `quality_bank_rerating` registry window = "High-ROE INDONESIAN & EM banks... (BBCA/BBRI/BMRI 2016-2023)". SMFG fails ALL THREE defining dimensions: not Indonesian, not EM, not high-ROE (10-11% vs BBCA/BBRI 18-22%). The EM re-rating engine is cost-of-funds EASING + credit normalization; SMFG's is rate-HIKING NIM — the opposite regime. n=20 EM-megabank cases say nothing about a Japanese megabank on BOJ normalization. The tell: the analyst KEEPS the archetype's favourable probability (0.48→0.42) but DISCARDS its magnitude (base_up 42%→22.4%) — precisely because a DM bank re-rating from ~1.7x cannot do what an EM bank re-rating from sub-1x did. If the magnitude doesn't transfer, neither does the probability. The screen's honest home is `momentum_continuation` (rate 0.50, horizon 0.75y), whose registry note reads: "a momentum-only thesis with no variant perception is an auto-kill" and "momentum crashes in sharp reversals" — a 0%-off-52w-high name to the letter. The bank METHOD is applied fine; the base-rate KEY is cherry-picked.

**5. Sizing math.** Ordering OK (kill 20.59 < entry 25.74 < target 31.50); down_pct −20.0% and up_pct +22.4% both reconcile to the levels within the ±3pp band. But the capital-return EV on the analyst's OWN numbers = 0.42×22.4 + 0.58×(−20) = **−2.19% over 3y — NEGATIVE**. expected_pct 4.2% is a 3-YEAR TOTAL kept positive only by 3×2.3% dividends — i.e. ~1.4%/yr. USD cash at 4.25%/yr compounds to ~13.3% over the same 3y at zero risk: the trade earns roughly ONE-THIRD of cash for taking Japanese-bank + EM-credit + USDJPY + momentum-reversal risk. On a negative capital-EV bet quarter-Kelly = 0 → the correct size is zero. It also fails the house capital hurdle (base_rates fr_duration_carry note: equity deserves capital only when the premium over risk-free exceeds ~4%/yr) — the premium here is ~ −2.9%/yr. The 0.5% fee_tax_drag is understated for a cross-border ADR (JPY dividend WHT 15.315%, ADR pass-through/custody, USD/JPY conversion, round-trip on a $47.7M-ADV mid-cap → realistically ~1-1.5pp). Exit-to-flat at the −20% kill, in the very scenario that triggers it (BOJ reversal / EM credit turn), at 20% ADV ($9.5M/day) gaps *through* −20% as liquidity evaporates.

**6. NEW disconfirming fact (not in thesis, sourced).** The June-2026 BOJ hike was a cost-push, geopolitics-driven move: wholesale inflation 6.3% (highest since Mar-2023) on the US-Israel/Iran oil shock, with the yen at ~160 (CNBC / Al Jazeera, 2026-06-16). The thesis's core NIM tailwind is riding IMPORTED SUPPLY-SHOCK inflation and yen weakness — not durable domestic demand-pull reflation. A cost-push hiking path is fragile and reversible: if oil normalizes or growth cracks, the BOJ pauses (the thesis's own kill), and a chunk of the japan_reflation momentum is a war premium. The clean "Tamura → 2% neutral" framing omits WHY the June hike happened. Supporting: third-party P/B prints ~1.45-1.46x (macrotrends Feb-26; companiesmarketcap May-26) vs the analyst's reconstructed 1.65-1.75x — a ~15% gap on the single input that flips EV from thin-positive to negative; the "analytical edge" is a precision claim on a number he cannot pin within 15%.

**7. Steelman the pre-mortem — unmentioned failure mode.** The pre-mortem never models USDJPY as a P&L driver, yet the USD target $31.50 was DERIVED at "USDJPY ~161.6." This is a JPY-earnings asset held via a USD ADR: if the BOJ hikes while the Fed cuts (the 2026-27 base case), USDJPY could move toward ~145 — a ~10% FX swing that shifts the USD target several dollars INDEPENDENT of the bank thesis. Unhedged FX noise of ±10-15% dwarfs the entire 4.2%/3y edge — the signal is smaller than the unmodeled FX variance. Second unmentioned mode: cross-shareholding realization gains (JPY446bn FY3/26; ~JPY224bn of one-offs) FADE mechanically as the strategic book runs down to <20% by Mar-29 — reported ROE can DECLINE even as core banking improves, quietly hollowing the "ROE durability" the re-rating requires.

**8. Anti-gaming inspection.** estimates_committed_at 14:28:13Z precedes the draft stamp 15:10:00Z — in order; the bottom-up section is price-free (pure JPY fundamentals), with market numbers confined to the valuation/target — consistent with "estimates before market data." No attack-log-in-waiting (the log was empty); no retro-edited or out-of-order estimates found. Clean on chronology. The one integrity concern is substantive, not temporal: an EM base-rate key knowingly applied to a Japanese bank (base_rate.source literally reads "IDX/EM megabank"), favourable probability kept and unfavourable magnitude dropped — convenient classification, per §4.

**9. VERDICT — KILL_RECOMMENDED.**
Single strongest sentence: *On the analyst's own numbers the capital-return EV is negative (−2.2% over 3y) and the entire thesis clears just +4.2% total over three years — about one-third of the ~13.3% risk-free cash earns over the same window — so the fund is being asked to take Japanese-bank, EM-credit, USDJPY and momentum-reversal risk in exchange for underperforming T-bills.*

sections.markdown:
**ANALYST_GLOBAL (Sloane) — Revision — 2026-07-12T03:24:16Z**

Responding to each numbered Bear point. Net effect of this revision: p_up cut, down-case widened, fee/tax drag corrected, and the archetype's fitness for this name conceded as doubtful. On the resulting numbers the thesis no longer clears a positive expected return -- see #9.

**0. Fact-check (ordinary-profit/net-income conflation; NII sensitivity shading).** Conceded, plainly. The committed Bottom-up section frames the "+JPY405.0bn YoY" / "EPS +36%" language alongside "record momentum" in a way that implies net-income growth of that magnitude; Drew is right that the ~+34% figure belongs to *ordinary* profit, and net-income growth was materially smaller (management's own core-business-ex-one-off delta was +JPY212bn on a JPY1,583bn base -- roughly +15-16% clean, not +34-36%). I cannot edit the Bottom-up section (committed, permanent per protocol) to fix the wording, so I flag the error here for the record and for the postmortem learned-rules queue: check a growth-rate figure against its exact P&L caption before quoting it, especially in a bank filing with multiple profit lines (ordinary vs. net vs. core-business-ex-one-off). Also conceded: the +JPY110bn/25bp NII sensitivity I used runs ~10% richer than the ~+JPY100bn/25bp figure in wider circulation. I have not re-based the model on that specific number, but the downward shading in #1/#4/#5 below absorbs more than a 10% haircut to it.

**1. Estimates at the widest honest error bar.** I did not simply adopt Drew's triplet; I rebuilt my own honest-bear case independently and it lands in the same place. Revised: p_up 0.35 (was 0.42), up_pct 20.0 (was 22.4 -- trimmed within the target-consistency band, since even the "up" case plausibly carries some multiple give-back rather than the full re-rating gap holding undiminished for 3 years), down_pct -25.0 (was -20.0; kill price moved to $19.31, see frontmatter and #4/#5), fee_tax_drag_pct 1.3 (was 0.5, see #5). Capital-only EV = 0.35x20.0 + 0.65x(-25.0) = -9.25% over 3y (more negative than my prior -2.19%, though less negative than Drew's -11.25% recompute on his own inputs). Full expected_pct = -3.65% over 3y (Drew's honest re-run got -4.85%). Different inputs, same conclusion: this is an expected loss, not a thin gain.

**2. Variant perception -- a correctly-priced premium, not a mispricing.** Conceded without reservation; this is the point that actually kills the thesis, not the arithmetic. My own residual-income warranted range (1.6-1.8x) and my own reconstructed current traded multiple (1.65-1.75x) overlap almost entirely -- by definition that is price = fair value, which is not a long. I should have flagged this as fatal in my own Variant Perception section rather than as a footnote that "most of the gap has closed." I also concede the consensus-target point: submitting a 3-year target (+22%) below the sell-side 1-year consensus extrapolated over 3 years is a tell that I am not bringing a variant view, I am bringing a lagged one. Re-tagging my edge claim honestly: the SMFG-plan-vs-Tamura-path observation is not distinguishable from the japan_reflation/momentum consensus already embedded in the stock's +55%/12m run -- it is the same trade with a residual-income label on it. I withdraw the edge claim; I do not have one that survives this attack.

**3. Catalyst.** Agreed this cuts against the thesis rather than being neutral. horizon=long without a dated catalyst is fine for a genuine compounder, but is a liability for a thesis that itself concedes (Disconfirming fact #3) the re-rating gap is "mostly closed" -- there is no mechanism left for time to work in the position's favor, only mechanisms (BOJ pause, NPL broadening, deposit-beta catch-up) that work against it. No estimate revision fixes an absent catalyst; noted as a structural weakness, not something patchable here.

**4. Base rate -- cherry-picked, not honest.** Conceded as the most serious methodological finding in the attack. The `quality_bank_rerating` registry window (the base-rate library) is explicitly EM/Indonesian banks re-rating off cost-of-funds *easing* and credit normalization from sub-1x P/BV (BBCA/BBRI/BMRI 2016-2023); SMFG is a developed-market bank already near its warranted multiple, on a rate-*hiking* NIM mechanism, with ROE roughly half the reference class. Those are close to opposite regimes. Drew is right that I kept the registry's favorable probability (0.48, lightly shaded to 0.42) while discarding its unfavorable magnitude (base_up_pct 42% swapped for my own DCF-derived 22.4%) -- a selective use of the archetype, not a disciplined one, even though I don't believe it was deliberate. I do not have authority under this Revision protocol to change the `archetype:` frontmatter key itself (only kill_criteria/ev_math/base_rate are mine to touch here); I flag explicitly for the Judge that reclassification -- most plausibly to `momentum_continuation` (rate 0.50, base_down_pct -22, horizon 0.75y, whose own registry note reads "a momentum-only thesis with no variant perception is an auto-kill") -- is a live, unresolved question this revision does not settle. In the interim I've cut p_up further, to 0.35, specifically because the probability I'm using has no clean reference class underneath it.

**5. Sizing math.** Conceded, and it gets worse under my own revised numbers, not better: capital-only EV is now -9.25% over 3y (was -2.19%), and total expected_pct is now -3.65% (was +4.2%) -- see frontmatter ev_math. I've raised fee_tax_drag_pct from 0.5 to 1.3 to reflect JPY dividend withholding tax (15.315%), ADR custody/pass-through cost, and USD/JPY round-trip conversion on a cross-border ADR, per Drew's citation -- 0.5 was not defensible for this instrument. On the liquidity-gap point: agreed that the scenario which trips the price kill (a BOJ reversal / EM-credit-turn shock) is precisely the kind of correlated, sharp move in which a 20%-ADV exit can gap through a clean kill level rather than fill at it; I've widened the kill trigger itself (see frontmatter) partly to build a margin against that gap rather than pretend the kill price is where the position actually exits in the tail scenario. I cannot fix execution-gap risk with a frontmatter number -- it belongs in PM sizing/order-ticket construction, and I'm flagging it in my sizing input to Harrison (PM_GLOBAL) as a reason for material downsizing if this proceeds at all.

**6. New disconfirming fact (cost-push BOJ hike).** Conceded as additional, independent bearish evidence -- not a flagged "new evidence:" fact favoring the long side, so it gives me no basis to raise anything; it cuts the other way. If the June 2026 hike is substantially a cost-push response to an oil shock and yen weakness rather than durable domestic demand-pull reflation, the core NII tailwind mechanism (BOJ keeps hiking, deposit beta stays lagged) is more fragile and reversible than I represented -- a growth scare or oil-price normalization plausibly stalls BOJ well short of Tamura's path, which my own kill criteria and pre-mortem already contemplate but under-weighted. I also accept the ~15% band on my own P/BV reconstruction (1.65-1.75x vs. third-party prints of 1.45-1.46x) as a real precision problem: on a name where the entire "already priced" finding in #2 turns on a multiple I can't pin within 15%, that uncertainty should compress my confidence, not expand it -- already reflected in the p_up cut to 0.35.

**7. Steelman the pre-mortem (unhedged FX; cross-shareholding gain fade).** Both conceded as real, unmentioned failure modes I should have modeled and didn't. Entry/kill/target are all USD ADR levels struck off a single USDJPY snapshot (~161.6); a BOJ-hikes/Fed-cuts convergence toward ~145 is a ~10-15% FX swing on those USD levels, larger than the entire revised edge and uncorrelated with whether the bank thesis itself is right. I have no clean way to build FX-conditionality into a single-price kill/target frontmatter, so I've treated the wider kill band and lower p_up as a blunt partial hedge against this unmodeled variance rather than claiming to have solved it, and I'm flagging to Harrison that unhedged FX exposure of this size relative to the edge is a reason to either hedge USDJPY explicitly at the PM stage or size well below what the raw EV would suggest. On cross-shareholding gain fade: agreed that reported ROE (10.4%/11.4%) is flattered by one-off equity-sale gains that mechanically shrink as the strategic-holdings book runs down toward  19.31 (down_pct -20.0% -> -25.0%; reasons #1/#4/#5 above).
- `base_rate.source`: appended the archetype-fitness caveat from #4 and updated the cited shaded p_up (0.42 -> 0.35).
- `ev_math`: p_up 0.42->0.35, up_pct 22.4->20.0, p_down 0.58->0.65, down_pct -20->-25.0, fee_tax_drag_pct 0.5->1.3, net_div_yield_pct_pa unchanged at 2.3, expected_pct 4.2->-3.65.
- Bottom-up estimates section, estimates_committed_at, stage_log, status, and verdict: untouched, per protocol.

**Routing note (procedural, not mine to decide).** Per the fund record Revision protocol, an ev_math field moving >20% relative sends the thesis back to Drew before Judge. down_pct (25% relative move), fee_tax_drag_pct (160% relative move, small in absolute pp terms), and expected_pct (sign flip, +4.2 -> -3.65) all exceed that bar. I'm flagging this for the orchestrator/Judge rather than routing it myself -- every change in this revision moves further against the trade, so I'd expect a further Bear pass to confirm rather than reverse KILL_RECOMMENDED, but the protocol step should not be skipped.

**BEAR RE-ATTACK — Drew — 2026-07-12T09:10:00Z — VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED**

Re-spawned for the mandatory re-attack pass (down_pct, fee_tax_drag_pct, and expected_pct all moved >20% relative in Revision #1). This is a verification pass on the revision, not a fresh nine-point attack — my original §0-§9 above stands verbatim and unedited.

**A. Honesty audit — did the Revision answer every point on its merits?** Yes, on all nine. §0: conceded plainly (ordinary-profit/net-income conflation, +10%-rich NII sensitivity), correctly noting the committed Bottom-up section can't be retro-edited so the correction is logged here instead of buried. §1: NOT copy-pasted from my triplet — independently rebuilt, and *disclosed*, not hidden, that it lands less severe than my own re-run (capital EV -9.25% vs my -11.25%; total -3.65% vs my -4.85%) — see C below for whether that gap is honest residual optimism. §2: fully conceded, including the consensus-vs-3y-target tell, with an explicit withdrawal of the one "genuine edge" claim — this is the correct kill point and it's stated as such. §3: conceded as structural, correctly not patched with an estimate tweak. §4: conceded as "the most serious methodological finding"; critically, the analyst does NOT unilaterally reclassify the archetype (outside Revision authority) but flags it as a live, unresolved question for the Judge — correct scope discipline, not a dodge. §5: conceded and shown to get worse under his own numbers, not better; fee_tax_drag_pct 1.3 sits inside my cited 1-1.5pp band, not lowballed to the floor. §6: taken as pure bear ammunition, "no basis to raise anything" — no spin. §7: both unmentioned failure modes (unhedged FX, cross-shareholding gain fade) fully conceded, with the analyst correctly declining to fake a frontmatter fix for FX-conditionality and instead pushing the hedging/downsizing call to Harrison. §8: correctly scoped. Nothing dodged, mischaracterized, or quietly hedged.

**B. Arithmetic re-derivation (independent).** Capital EV = 0.35×20.0 + 0.65×(-25.0) = 7.00 - 16.25 = **-9.25%**, matches. Total expected_pct via the same capital_EV + 3×net_div_yield_pct_pa - fee_tax_drag_pct formula implicit in both my original entry and this revision: -9.25 + 6.90 - 1.30 = **-3.65%**, matches exactly -- and it's the identical formula that reproduces my original -4.85% and the analyst's original +4.2%, i.e. no formula-switching across passes to manufacture a better-looking number. Kill price 25.74×(1-0.25) = 19.305 ≈ **19.31**, matches to the cent. p_down = 1-0.35 = 0.65, correct. up_pct 20.0 vs. the unchanged target's price-implied gain of 22.4% is a 2.4pp trim inside the ±3pp lint band, and it cuts against the trade, not for it. No arithmetic slippage found anywhere.

**C. Where the revision, if anything, still UNDERSTATES the damage.** (1) `exit_plan.target` ($31.50) is untouched -- correctly outside Revision authority -- but it's still built on warranted P/BV 1.80x, the TOP of the analyst's own 1.6-1.8x fair-value band, at the exact moment §2 concedes price already sits at 1.65-1.75x, near that same top edge. An "up case" that still requires re-rating to the very top of a range you've just admitted is basically already reached is not a clean 20% upside -- it smuggles in a sliver of the re-rating §2 disclaims. A properly cleaned up-case (pure ROTE×(1-payout) book compounding, no further multiple expansion) is closer to my original 18%, which would move capital EV to roughly -9.95% and total expected_pct to roughly -4.35%. (2) down_pct -25.0% was set to the pre-mortem's own midpoint (20-30%) rather than weighted toward the worse end the pre-mortem's own language argues for ("given the EM overseas book") -- why I used -27% originally. Both residuals push the same direction: more negative, not less. I find nothing in this revision that flatters the trade in the other direction. Honest floor is probably closer to my original -4.85% than the restated -3.65%.

**D. Anti-gaming — anything new from the revision itself?** No. stage_log, status, verdict, estimates_committed_at are genuinely untouched (checked against the diff); the "Frontmatter changes made this revision" list is complete and matches the actual changes, nothing unlisted. Revision timestamp (03:24:16Z) is chronologically after both estimates_committed_at and my attack stamp, in order. One PRE-EXISTING anomaly, not created by this revision and missed on my own original pass: stage_log's `attacked` stamp (2026-07-11T14:47:19Z) is chronologically BEFORE the `draft` stamp (2026-07-11T15:10:00Z) it's supposed to follow -- a 23-minute inversion. Flagging verbatim for the Judge's stage_log chain-check (fund record point 2); it predates this revision so it doesn't move today's verdict, but it shouldn't be waved through uninspected either.

**E. VERDICT — KILL_RECOMMENDED.** Strongest sentence: *This is a rare fully-honest revision -- every one of my nine points was conceded on its merits and the new arithmetic re-derives to the cent -- but the two places the analyst didn't touch (a target still priced to the top of his own fair-value band, and a through-cycle down_pct parked at the pre-mortem's midpoint rather than its own worse-weighted end) both cut further against the trade, so the honest expected loss is probably closer to my original -4.85%-over-3y than the restated -3.65%, and either number is a loss against a risk-free ~13% for taking Japanese-bank, EM-credit, USDJPY, and momentum-reversal risk with no variant perception left standing.*

**JUDGE VERDICT — Aldrich — 2026-07-12T04:40:15Z — KILL (reason_tag: process)**

No the kill ledger exists yet, so there is no calibration-drift record to correct against this session. Lint passes structurally (word-count warning only), but the stage_log chain fails independent verification: the `attacked` stamp (2026-07-11T14:47:19Z) precedes the `draft` stamp (2026-07-11T15:10:00Z) by 23 minutes — the identical hand-rounded-draft-timestamp defect already flagged on sibling T-GLOBAL-NVO-001 in this batch — and the log carries no `revised`/`re-attacked` entries for the 2026-07-12 revision cycle; re-running the thesis linter against a status:judged copy confirms it fails "stage_log timestamps not monotonic," silent today only because the monotonic check doesn't gate on status:draft. Per protocol, any stage_log ordering violation is a KILL with reason_tag process regardless of merits, and the merits independently agree: (a) p_up 0.35 sits 13pp/27% below the quality_bank_rerating registry rate (0.48) on an archetype the analyst himself concedes is a near-opposite-regime mismatch (EM cost-of-funds-easing re-rating vs. a DM rate-hiking NIM story), keeping the archetype's favorable probability while discarding its unfavorable magnitude — and Bear's proposed "honest home," momentum_continuation, would auto-kill on its own registry note given the analyst's explicit withdrawal of variant perception; (b) every load-bearing input is document-cited (Bear's fact-check found no fabrication, only a conceded ordinary-profit/net-income mislabel); (c) the thesis does not survive Drew's strongest sentence — restated, even the analyst's own honestly-rebuilt numbers clear only -3.65% over 3y (Bear's independent re-derivation: -4.85%) against ~13% risk-free cash, with the one claimed edge (SMFG's sub-consensus BOJ-terminal assumption) conceded to be indistinguishable from the japan_reflation consensus trade already priced into the stock's 0%-off-52-week-high run — a consensus-quarantine problem, not a variant view. No unflagged raise of p_up/up_pct/target occurred in the revision (every changed figure moved against the trade); entry and exit levels are valuation-anchored (residual-income/warranted-P/BV), not price-history-anchored. This kill is dispositive on process; base_rate, valuation, and fragile_estimates would each independently kill it on the merits alone.
